sent.text: I pressed the tired wedge down on The Wet Paper Sky, hoping the thin lines would bite while the card hummed warm, but I see there is no such sky there at all. You ask if the air above feels like a heavy lid or empty space, and I tell you that it presses down just enough to make the flat edges feel too thin to hold anything. I set a dark tree plateau beside The Slipping Wedge to catch the lazy slip, hoping a second flat edge can find a softer place to rest. If you say the weight is real, I will trust your word to keep the dot safe while I wait for the roof to finish deciding if it is there.

dream: The card hummed warm at fifty-three while I pressed the tired wedge down again. The Wet Paper Sky felt heavy, pressing against the Flat Weigher until the thin edge finally bit. I swapped a square stump for a round one, then pressed them both together to make a single, wobbling corner. The fence leaned wrong, and I pressed harder until the air grew thick as wet paper. When I opened my eyes to the dream, the heavy lid was upside down, waiting to press the tired slip sideways.
